deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): Riemann is working on the motion of a homogeneous liquid ellipsoid, the topic of his 1861 Göttingen memoir 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines flüssigen gleichartigen Ellipsoides'. The semi-axes are l, m, n with lmn = const. The potential-type integral is u = ∫_0^∞ ds/Δ, where Δ = sqrt((l^2+s)(m^2+s)(n^2+s)). The equations of motion have the form l l'' − m m'' = ½(l ∂u/∂l − m ∂u/∂m), and similarly with n. He introduces log-axis-ratio variables α, β with d log m − d log l = ½ dα and d log n − d log l = ½ dβ. Hence d log l = −(1/6)(dα + dβ), d log m = (1/6)(2dα − dβ), d log n = (1/6)(2dβ − dα). He also rewrites u through an incomplete elliptic integral v(x, y) and computes the derivatives of u with respect to log l, log m, log n by the chain rule. The lower lines of the previous page begin expanding the kinetic terms, of the form −(1/6)((1±a)·… + (∂β/∂α)(1∓a))·α'^2. Here a and b appear to be coefficients, possibly the proportionality factors in the ansatz dβ/dα or second-order terms; this identification is mine and uncertain.

This page:
(1) Two parallel expressions are written:
  −(1/6)[(1−a) ∂²p/∂α² α'^2 · (1−b) + ∂p/∂α · (1+2b)]
  −(1/6)[(1+2b) ∂²p/∂α² α'^2 · (1+2a) + ∂p/∂α · (1−a)].
  Here p is an unknown function of α; the 'x' in the transcription is the letter α. Each line has a second-order term with product coefficient (1−a)(1−b), respectively (1+2b)(1+2a), and a first-order term with coefficient (1+2b), respectively (1−a). The structure mirrors the 1/6-weights (2, −1, −1) from the log-axis decomposition.
(2) A start '(1−a)(1−b) −' is struck out and rewritten as (1−a)(1−b) − (1+2b)(1+2a).
(3) This is evaluated (expansion mine): (1−a)(1−b) = 1 − a − b + ab and (1+2a)(1+2b) = 1 + 2a + 2b + 4ab. The difference is −3a − 3b − 3ab.
(4) The resulting term is written as −(1/6) ∂²p/∂α² α'^2 (−3a − 3b − 3ab), i.e. the difference of the second-order terms of the two lines. The first-order terms (1+2b) and (1−a) are not combined on the page.
(5) Left half: isolated beginnings '∂v/∂y =' and '(∂y/∂l)·l'. These are the start of the chain-rule computation of l ∂u/∂l via u = v·(l^2−m^2)^(−1/2) and y = 1 − m^2/l^2, continuing the previous page. They are not carried out here.

Purpose: forming the difference of the two equations, l l'' − m m'' versus l l'' − n n'', expressed in the α-variables, to obtain the reduced equation of motion, perhaps for small oscillations or stability. Note the next page is a draft letter mentioning Livorno and Riemann's wife, which dates the sheet to 1862 or later despite the '1853' bundle label.
errors: In the image the sign of the 3ab term appears overwritten/corrected; the correct final value is −3ab.
The first-derivative terms ∂p/∂α·(1+2b) and ∂p/∂α·(1−a) are not carried into the combined line, so the combination is incomplete as written (the page breaks off).
The first line's bracket is unbalanced in the manuscript; this is a notational looseness only.

results.what: Elementary polynomial identity (1−a)(1−b) − (1+2a)(1+2b) = −3(a + b + ab), used to combine two equations of motion for the ellipsoid axes in log-ratio variables
results.modern_name: algebraic simplification within the dynamics of a liquid ellipsoid (Dirichlet–Dedekind–Riemann problem)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's 1861 memoir on the liquid ellipsoid (after Dirichlet 1857/1860, Dedekind)

results.what: Chain-rule setup for l ∂u/∂l with u expressed through an incomplete elliptic integral v(x, y)
results.modern_name: derivatives of the ellipsoidal potential coefficients (index symbols)
